description: Experience the true taste of Liguria with our authentic Focaccia Genovese. This beloved Italian flatbread, kissed with fragrant rosemary and rich olive oil, boasts an irresistibly crispy crust and a tender, airy interior. Perfect as an appetizer, a side, or a delightful snack on its own.

ingredients.notes: plus extra for drizzling and pan

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine the warm water, granulated sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Combine Dry and Wet Ingredients
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the bread flour and fine sea salt. Pour the activated yeast mixture and 30ml of the extra virgin olive oil into the flour mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy, cohesive dough forms.

instructions.title: Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. It should feel soft and pliable.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean large bowl with a drizzle of olive oil. Place the kneaded dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare Pan and Dimple
instructions.text: Generously oil a 30x40cm (12x16 inch) baking sheet with extra virgin olive oil. Gently punch down the risen dough and transfer it to the prepared baking sheet. Slowly press and stretch the dough with your fingertips to fill the pan, creating characteristic dimples across the surface. Drizzle with the remaining 20ml of olive oil, sprinkle with sea salt, and scatter the chopped fresh rosemary.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Bake
instructions.text: Cover the baking sheet loosely with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let the focaccia rise for another 30-45 minutes in a warm place. Meanwhile, preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F).

instructions.title: Bake and Serve
instructions.text: Bake the focaccia in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until it is golden brown on top and the bottom sounds hollow when tapped. Remove from the oven, and if desired, drizzle with a little more fresh extra virgin olive oil. Let it cool slightly on a wire rack before slicing and serving warm.

tips: For an extra crispy crust, preheat your baking sheet in the oven for 10 minutes before carefully transferring the dough onto it.
Do not skimp on good quality extra virgin olive oil; it is the soul of a true Focaccia Genovese and contributes immensely to its flavor and texture.
If not serving immediately, store leftover focaccia in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in the oven or a toaster oven for best results.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast of Italy, where one of the simplest yet most profoundly satisfying breads was born: Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil. This iconic Italian flatbread, known for its irresistible aroma, golden crust, and tender, airy interior, is a testament to the power of a few high-quality ingredients. More than just bread, it’s an experience – a warm, fragrant invitation to savor the authentic taste of Italian baking. With its distinctive dimples cradling pools of rich olive oil and fragrant rosemary, it’s no wonder this particular focaccia has captured hearts around the globe.

## What is Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil?

At its heart, Focaccia Genovese is a classic Italian flatbread originating from Genoa, the capital of the Liguria region. Unlike some thicker, more doughy focaccias, the Genovese style is typically thinner, with a wonderfully crisp bottom and a soft, airy crumb. What truly sets it apart is the generous use of olive oil – it’s integral to the dough, slathered onto the pan, and drizzled lavishly over the top before baking. This not only imparts incredible flavor but also contributes to its signature texture. The characteristic dimples, pressed into the dough before its final rise, are not just for aesthetics; they serve as perfect little reservoirs for the olive oil and coarse sea salt, ensuring every bite is bursting with savory goodness. The addition of fresh rosemary is a classic and beloved pairing, its pungent, piney notes complementing the richness of the olive oil beautifully. This isn't just any focaccia; it's *the* Focaccia Genovese, a masterclass in simplicity and flavor.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Focaccia Genovese requires a short list of ingredients, emphasizing quality over quantity. Each component plays a crucial role in achieving that perfect texture and taste.

*   **Strong Bread Flour (approx. 500g):** High-protein flour is essential for developing the gluten structure needed for a chewy yet tender crumb.
*   **Warm Water (approx. 350-400ml):** Around 100-110°F (38-43°C) is ideal for activating the yeast.
*   **Active Dry Yeast (7g or 1 packet):** The leavening agent that gives the focaccia its lift and airy texture.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil (at least 100ml, plus more for drizzling):** This is non-negotiable. Use a high-quality, flavorful olive oil. It’s fundamental to the dough, the pan, and the topping.
*   **Fine Sea Salt (10g for dough):** Enhances the flavor of the dough.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt (for topping):** Provides a delightful textural contrast and bursts of salinity on the crust.
*   **Fresh Rosemary (2-3 sprigs):** Chopped or left as small sprigs for the topping, its aromatic essence is key to Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil.
*   **A pinch of sugar (optional):** To help activate the yeast faster.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Focaccia Genovese is a rewarding process that requires patience but yields incredible results.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and an optional pinch of sugar. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the bread flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Pour in about 50ml of extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy, sticky dough forms.
3.  **Knead (or Stretch and Fold):** Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth, elastic, and less sticky. Alternatively, perform a series of "stretch and folds" in the bowl over 30-minute intervals for about 1.5-2 hours total, keeping the dough covered.
4.  **First Rise:** Place the dough in a large, lightly oiled bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally coat a 9x13 inch (or similar size) baking sheet with extra virgin olive oil – don't be shy! This creates the signature crispy bottom.
6.  **Shape and Dimple:** Gently transfer the risen dough to the prepared baking sheet. Gently stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. Drizzle generously with more olive oil. Using your fingertips, press deep dimples all over the surface of the dough. The dimples should go almost all the way down to the pan.
7.  **Dress and Second Rise:** Sprinkle coarse sea salt evenly over the dimpled dough and scatter the fresh rosemary sprigs or chopped leaves. Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise again in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
8.  **Bake:** Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake the Focaccia Genovese for 20-30 minutes, or until golden brown on top and cooked through. The bottom should be deeply golden and crispy.
9.  **Finish:** Once out of the oven, you can drizzle with a final touch of fresh olive oil for extra sheen and flavor. Let it cool on the pan for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack. Slice and serve warm.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect Focaccia Genovese is all about attention to detail and embracing the Italian philosophy of quality ingredients.

*   **Embrace the Stickiness:** Focaccia dough is typically high in hydration, making it quite sticky. Don't be tempted to add too much extra flour during kneading, as this will result in a dense, dry bread. A sticky dough is your friend; it's the secret to a light, airy crumb.
*   **Quality Olive Oil is Key:** This cannot be stressed enough. Since olive oil is such a dominant flavor, invest in a good quality extra virgin olive oil. It makes all the difference in the world.
*   **Deep Dimples:** When dimpling, don't be shy! Press your fingers firmly into the dough, almost touching the bottom of the pan. These deep wells are crucial for trapping the olive oil and sea salt, creating pockets of intense flavor and preventing the dough from puffing up too much like regular bread.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Oil:** From oiling the bowl for the first rise, to generously coating the baking pan, to drizzling over the top before and after baking, olive oil is fundamental. It contributes to the crispy crust, tender interior, and rich flavor.
*   **Warm Environment for Rising:** Yeast loves warmth. Ensure your dough rises in a consistently warm, draft-free place for optimal activity and a beautifully airy texture.
*   **Listen to Your Dough:** The rising times are estimates. Pay attention to the dough itself – it should be visibly doubled in size for the first rise and noticeably puffy for the second.
*   **Hot Oven, Quick Bake:** A hot oven ensures a quick bake, creating a crispy exterior before the interior dries out.

## Serving Suggestions

The versatility of Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is one of its most appealing characteristics. It shines in numerous culinary settings:

*   **As an Appetizer:** Serve warm with a side of good quality balsamic vinegar for dipping, or alongside a platter of antipasti, cured meats, and cheeses.
*   **Soup and Salad Companion:** Its hearty yet airy texture makes it perfect for sopping up broths from minestrone or lentil soup, or as an accompaniment to a fresh green salad.
*   **Sandwich Bread:** Slice it horizontally and fill it with your favorite Italian deli meats, cheeses, roasted vegetables, or pesto for an extraordinary sandwich.
*   **Simple Snack:** Enjoy it on its own, perhaps with just a light drizzle of fresh olive oil, appreciating its pure, unadulterated flavor.
*   **Breakfast Treat:** Believe it or not, a slice of Focaccia Genovese with a cup of coffee makes for a delightful, savory breakfast.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is perfect as is, it also serves as an excellent canvas for culinary creativity.

*   **Other Toppings:** Experiment with other toppings. Olives (Kalamata or Castelvetrano), halved cherry tomatoes, caramelized onions, thinly sliced garlic, or a sprinkle of dried oregano or thyme are all fantastic additions. You can even combine a few!
*   **Flour Blends:** For a slightly different texture, you can substitute a portion of the bread flour (up to 25%) with whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor, or semolina flour for an even crispier crust.
*   **Infused Olive Oil:** Take your focaccia to the next level by using garlic-infused olive oil, or chili-infused oil for a subtle kick.
*   **Sweet Focaccia:** While less common for the Genovese style, some regions make sweet focaccia with sugar, raisins, or even fruit. This would be a significant departure from the savory classic, but interesting to explore.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While achieving the exact same texture can be challenging, a high-quality gluten-free bread flour blend can be used. You may need to adjust the water content slightly and expect a denser crumb.

Mastering the art of Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a journey into the heart of Italian baking. With its alluring aroma, exquisite texture, and robust flavor, it’s more than just a bread; it’s a celebration of simple, honest ingredients transformed into something truly extraordinary. Whether you’re an experienced baker or a curious beginner, the satisfaction of pulling a golden, fragrant Focaccia Genovese from your oven is a joy that’s hard to beat. Give it a try, and let the flavors of Liguria transport you.
